questions.question: As per the OSI layer-wise protocol list, which protocol belongs to the Session Layer?
questions.explanation: Session Layer protocols are PPTP, PAP, NetBIOS and ASP. MIME is a Presentation Layer protocol, SLIP is Data Link and IGMP is Network Layer.

questions.question: What is the 8's complement of the octal number 5670?
questions.explanation: 8's complement = 8^n - number. For 5670 (n = 4): 7777 - 5670 = 2107 (7's complement), then add 1 to get 2110.

questions.question: Which malware identification method runs a suspicious file inside a virtual environment and observes its behaviour?
questions.explanation: Sandbox detection executes the suspicious file in a virtual environment, so it cannot access real system resources while its behaviour is analysed.

questions.question: According to Python's version history, which release had 33 keywords?
questions.explanation: Python 2.0 (2000) had 30 keywords, Python 3.0 (2008) had 33 keywords and Python 3.8 (2019) had 35 keywords.

questions.concept: Number of pages from logical address bits
questions.question: A system has a 27-bit logical address, a 21-bit physical address and a page size of 1 KB. How many pages are there in the logical address space?
questions.explanation: Page size 1 KB = 2^10, so the offset d = 10 bits. Page bits P = 27 - 10 = 17, giving 2^17 = 131072 pages. 2048 (2^11) is the number of frames.

questions.concept: Models equivalent to a Turing machine
questions.question: Which of the following is described as an equivalent model of a Turing machine?
questions.explanation: Register machines, multi-tape and multi-track Turing machines are listed as equivalent models of the Turing machine. Finite automata, PDAs and LBAs are less powerful.

questions.question: A developer must remove every row from a table quickly while keeping the table structure, without using a WHERE clause. Which command fits?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE deletes all rows faster and keeps the table structure; WHERE is not used. DELETE removes selected rows with WHERE, and DROP removes the whole table.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four dimensions of the Cloud Cube Model (CCM)?
questions.explanation: The Cloud Cube Model classifies networks as Internal/External, Insourced/Outsourced, Proprietary/Open and Perimeterized/De-perimeterized. Public/Private describes deployment types, not CCM dimensions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector image format?
questions.explanation: Vector images are made from mathematical paths; examples include SVG, EPS, WMF and AI. BMP, TIFF and GIF are raster (bitmap) formats.

questions.question: What is the condition called when an attempt is made to push an element into a stack that is already full?
questions.explanation: Overflow occurs when trying to push an element into a full stack. Underflow occurs when trying to remove an element from an empty stack.

questions.question: Which of the following are functions of the OSI Presentation Layer? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Presentation Layer functions are translation, encryption, decryption and compression. Dialog control belongs to the Session Layer and routing to the Network Layer.

questions.question: Which term refers to the measure of interdependence between software modules?
questions.explanation: Coupling measures interdependence between modules, while cohesion measures the functional strength of a module. Good design has low coupling and strong cohesion.

questions.question: Which network threat, also known as sniffing, is the secret capture and analysis of network traffic, which may be analysed later?
questions.explanation: Snooping is the secret capture and analysis of network traffic and is also known as sniffing. Eavesdropping is real-time interception of private communication.

questions.question: What is the condition called when the CPU spends more time swapping pages, resulting in low CPU utilization due to a high number of page faults?
questions.explanation: Thrashing is when the CPU spends more time swapping pages between memory, resulting in low CPU utilization; it is caused by a high number of page faults.

questions.question: Which Python keyword is used for debugging?
questions.explanation: assert is used for debugging. pass executes nothing, yield returns values from a generator and with is used for the exception-handling context.

questions.question: Which law of Boolean algebra is expressed by the identity A + A·B = A?
questions.explanation: The Absorption Law states A + A·B = A and A + A'·B = A + B. The Idempotent Law is A + A = A, and the Annulment Law is A + 1 = 1.

questions.question: Which principle states that any function computable by an algorithm is computable by a Turing machine?
questions.explanation: Church's thesis states that any function computable by an algorithm is computable by a Turing machine, linking algorithms and Turing machines.

questions.question: SQL belongs to which generation of programming languages?
questions.explanation: SQL is a 4th generation language, along with FoxPro, Access and Oracle. 3rd generation covers languages like C, C++ and Java.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a thin client?
questions.explanation: A thin client relies on a central server for most computation; examples are Gmail, Office 365 and search engines. MS Word, Notepad++ and MS Outlook are thick clients.

questions.question: Which IEEE standard is associated with WiMAX?
questions.explanation: IEEE 802.16 is WiMAX (Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access). 802.11 is WLAN, 802.14 is cable modems and 802.15.1 is Bluetooth.

questions.question: In the operator precedence rules used for expression conversion, which operator group is evaluated from right to left?
questions.explanation: Exponentiation (^) is evaluated right to left. Parentheses, multiplication/division and addition/subtraction are evaluated left to right.

questions.question: In multimedia, which effect is an animation that changes one image slowly into another?
questions.explanation: Morphing is animation that changes one image slowly into another, while warping is distortion of one static image to another.

questions.question: In C++, which operator is used to release memory that was allocated with new?
questions.explanation: C++ allocates memory with the new operator and releases it with delete. C uses malloc()/calloc() to allocate and free() to release.

questions.question: A full adder is constructed using:

options.A: Two half adders and one OR gate
options.B: Two half adders and one AND gate
options.C: One half adder and two OR gates
options.D: Three half adders and one XOR gate

questions.explanation: A full adder adds three inputs and produces two outputs; it is constructed using 2 half adders and 1 OR gate.
